about: The second-opinion rule in driver.json, `opinions` and `workspaceOpinions` (XAGENT1a, D155 point 3, the second-agent design §2.2-§2.6): the table both twins hold, the CLI's opinions.ts (through driverconfig.ts) and the driver's OpinionRules. `read`: a file's text, a repository and its workspace (null is none, read as the default one), and what resolves: the source (`repository` or `workspace`, null for nothing) and the rule as kept, as JSON text (`false` is none here). `problems`: what a repository's entry holds, as JSON text, and the first problem said, null for none. `says`: a rule as kept, as JSON text, the reviewers it lists that are the working agent's own family, and the sentences each door says as it is set, in order. `edits`: a file's text, an edit as JSON (`repository` or `workspace`, then `set` with any of `reviewers`, `on`, `required`, `verify`, `minutes` and `recheck`, `none`, or `clear`), and either the file's `opinions` and `workspaceOpinions` once written, as JSON text with an absent map left out, or the refusal, nothing written. `families`: the agent a machine's work runs on, a reviewer, and whether they are one family, by each side's own declarations of an adapter's owner (AGT7) and maker. `pluginFamilies` (XAGENT1b2, design §3.1): the same, on a machine whose home holds plugins, each a folder and its `plugin.json` text, read by each side's own catalogue, so a contributing plugin's harness is judged by its `accountOf` and its declared `maker`, and a refused plugin contributes nothing.

says: none here
false
No second opinion here, whatever its workspace says: no other agent reads work here before it lands.
one reviewer before landing
{"on":["landing"],"reviewers":["codex-acp"]}
Before work here lands, `codex-acp` reads it, in a copy of its own that nothing is taken back from; its findings go to the session that did the work, and to you.
If no reviewer can read it, you are told so, and nothing waits.
One pass takes at most 20 minutes.
the design's repository rule
{"on":["landing","steps"],"reviewers":["codex-acp"],"verify":true,"minutes":30}
Before work here lands, `codex-acp` reads it, in a copy of its own that nothing is taken back from; its findings go to the session that did the work, and to you.
It reads each step's work here too, before the chain's next step starts.
It may build and run what this repository declares safe, in that copy.
If no reviewer can read it, you are told so, and nothing waits.
One pass takes at most 30 minutes.
the design's workspace rule
{"on":["landing"],"reviewers":["codex-acp","dsh"],"required":true}
Before work here lands, `codex-acp`, else `dsh`, reads it, in a copy of its own that nothing is taken back from; its findings go to the session that did the work, and to you.
If no reviewer can read it, the work waits for you.
One pass takes at most 20 minutes.
